newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Volatility trades executed in UK's FTSE.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Volatility trades executed in UK's FTSE.

text.p: Volatility and spread trades were popular in UK equity options as the stock market reversed early losses and grudgingly shuffled higher, dealers said.
In index options, the main deals were put spreads hedged by FTSE futures which rely on changes in stock market volatility to make money.

The biggest deal by mid-afternoon was in European-style FTSE 100 index where 1,000 September 3825 puts were sold at 6p and 1,000 September 4125 puts bought at 19p against buying June FTSE futures at 4665.

If the spread is properly hedged and if the market falls, then losses from the futures should be offset by a widening of the spread and if the market rallies, then losses from the spread as it shrinks in value will be offset by the long futures.
But, provided the options volatility increases sufficiently, the deal will make a profit.

Another volatility deal involved selling a long-dated diagonal spread against futures and it concerned buying December 4,425 puts at 88p, selling 500 March 4325 FTSE puts at 92 against selling FTSE futures at 4673. By 1540 GMT, cash FTSE was up 16.9 at 4658.9 while June futures were up 16 at 4673.

Over in stock options, one of the larger deals was in British Telecommunications where a calendar call spread was crossed. It concerned 2,000 August 460 calls traded at 15p and 2,000 February 460 calls traded at 22p.

The buyer of the spread expects volatility of BT shares to decrease as the shares reach 460p upto August expiry -- when the spread will be at its widest -- and then for the stock to climb higher so that the long February calls turn in a profit.
The seller expects the opposite to occur.
